title: Copying James P. Johnson piano rolls
summary: Randolph copied James P. Johnson's Carolina Shout from rolls but could not stretch the left-hand tenths.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, no, I didn't get a chance to hear him. But I'll tell you who I did hear, and it was James P. Johnson.
James P. Yes. Well, I didn't get a chance to see him, but I heard -- you know --
Yeah, his piano rolls, because I used to sit and copy that.
Yes. You know, he had a way of tenting, and I couldn't make those tenths. He'd make the tenths with one hand and he would go --
And while that tenths is going on this righthand is going --
And you would be surprised, (unintelligible) try to get that but, see, I couldn't make that. That was some stretch, because the best I could do would have to break it and it wouldn't sound --
-- yeah, and break that by rolling my hand. And it wouldn't sound as good.
